title: Wythall Wellington Memorial
crew_summary: 6 crew — 3 killed on impact, 1 died 11 January 1942, 2 injured
memorial_details: Memorial tree and plaque in a private location at Wythall, Worcestershire.
narrative: Wellington W5356 of 12 (B) Squadron, coded PH-T, departed Binbrook at 0438 on 9 January 1942 for Cherbourg. The aircraft was damaged over the target and lost its port engine. The pilot attempted to land at RAF Wythall, a Balloon Command station with no runways, and struck trees while circling at 0915. The aircraft crashed and burned. Three crew were killed on impact and a fourth died on 11 January 1942; two were injured but survived.
cause_of_loss: Battle damage — port engine lost over target; crashed while attempting emergency landing at RAF Wythall

sources.title: Chorley, W.R. — Bomber Command Losses Vol. 3
